name: registry.wait
description: Block until a registry key changes (any of: subkey added/removed, value added/removed/modified). Returns when the change fires or the timeout expires.

timeout_ms.description: Maximum wait in milliseconds. Returns ERR timeout if no change occurs within this window. Default 30 seconds.

watch_subtree.description: If true, fire on changes anywhere in the key's subtree (subkeys, sub-subkeys). Without this, only direct changes to `path` itself trigger.

changed.description: True when the change notification fired. (Reserved for future semantics; today the response is always true on success.)

x-implementations.name: reg_notify_change_key_value
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegNotifyChangeKeyValue` with `REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_NAME | REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_SET | REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTES | REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_SECURITY`. Uses an event handle + `WaitForMultipleObjects(event, connection_cancel_event, timeout)` for clean cancellation on connection close.

windows-modern.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue with all four change classes. WaitForMultipleObjects integrates the event with a connection-cancel event for shutdown semantics.

windows-classic.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue available since NT 3.1. Win 9x has a more limited registry-change API; the classic agent on 9x falls back to a polling read loop (RegEnumValue + comparison).
